subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core cross-session run-event observation API for peer `sessions_send` runs, and if so should it be exposed as `sessions_subscribe`, a `sessions_send` progress option, or only a narrower ACP/subagent path?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent API shape decides authorization, redaction, event retention, replay, and channel-visible delivery behavior across session boundaries.

options.title: Design `sessions_subscribe`
options.body: Add a bounded, redacted, authorization-checked `agent.events` or equivalent read API and expose it through a separate agent tool.

options.title: Extend `sessions_send`
options.body: Add an opt-in progress mode to `sessions_send` if maintainers prefer one combined send-and-observe surface.

options.title: Limit to ACP parent streams
options.body: Keep live progress only on the existing parent-owned ACP/subagent paths and document that peer `sessions_send` remains final/accepted-only.

recommendation.title: Design `sessions_subscribe`
recommendation.body: Add a bounded, redacted, authorization-checked `agent.events` or equivalent read API and expose it through a separate agent tool.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for `sessions_send`, `agent.wait`, and gateway session behavior points to steipete.
